stories.name: Intel Terafab partnerships
stories.blurb: Intel is emerging as a key chip partner in Elon Musk's Terafab AI chip venture while also exploring a U.S. memory chip manufacturing deal with SK Hynix.

stories.name: Intel stock turnaround
stories.blurb: Investors and analysts are debating whether Intel's surging stock and foundry ambitions make it a genuine turnaround play or an overvalued bet.

stories.name: AMD Stock Surge
stories.blurb: AMD's stock has crossed $1 trillion amid growing AI optimism, a Microsoft partnership, and debate over whether it remains a good buy.

stories.name: Intel stock crash
stories.blurb: Intel shares suffered their worst one-day plunge in decades after the chipmaker issued weak fourth-quarter guidance, citing a persistent PC slowdown that also dragged down other chip stocks.

stories.name: AI chip stock rally
stories.blurb: Investors are debating whether the surging valuations of AI chipmakers like NVIDIA and Marvell are justified by future growth or due for a pullback.

stories.name: Apple Ditching Qualcomm
stories.blurb: Apple is gradually replacing Qualcomm's modem chips with its own in-house designs, raising questions about Qualcomm's future revenue and stock performance.

past.name: AI Chip Selloff
past.blurb: A broad global selloff in AI and semiconductor stocks, driven by fading enthusiasm for AI trade and weak guidance, has pushed the Nasdaq into correction.

past.name: Intel stock activity
past.blurb: Intel is repeatedly among the most actively traded stocks in the S&P 500 across daily sessions.

past.name: ASML AI chip demand
past.blurb: ASML is ramping up EUV lithography production and attracting investor attention as surging AI chip demand drives competition among major semiconductor players.

past.name: AI Chip Market Growth
past.blurb: A collection of market reports highlighting how AI, 5G, and edge computing are driving rapid growth across semiconductors, chipsets, and related hardware markets where Intel competes.

past.name: Intel SK Hynix talks
past.blurb: Intel and SK Hynix are reportedly in talks for a deal to manufacture memory chips in the U.S., sending both companies' shares higher.

past.name: Intel-SK Hynix Ohio Deal
past.blurb: Intel is reportedly in talks with SK Hynix to manufacture memory chips at Intel's underused Ohio fab, boosting Intel's stock alongside a separate $15 billion capital raise for AI chip growth.

past.name: AI chip selloff
past.blurb: A broad selloff in AI-related chip and memory stocks, driven by bubble fears and weak guidance, is dragging down markets worldwide.

past.name: Meta Muse AI Chip Rally
past.blurb: Meta's new Muse AI agent sparked expectations of increased CPU demand, sending Intel, AMD, and Arm shares sharply higher amid broader moves in the AI chip sector.

past.name: Tech Stocks Roundup

16.text: Musk floated a $1 trillion cost for his Terafab chip plant without disputing it, though only a fraction has an official price tag. SK Hynix profit fell 58%, bearing on Intel only as semiconductor-sector context.

7.text: Intel shares fell sharply after weak Q4 guidance and a factory incident, despite strongest data-center growth in 15 years. Analysts now debate valuation, with some upgrading to bullish on 2027 growth and recovery potential.

11.text: AMD beat Q3 estimates with record data-center revenue, guided to roughly $17 billion next quarter, and signed a 6-gigawatt Meta GPU deal, yet the stock remains well below its October high amid inventory and valuation concerns. Intel is barely mentioned; the coverage concerns AMD's AI-driven gains and competitive server-CPU share.

18.text: Intel shares fell sharply on a weak fourth-quarter revenue outlook and supply constraints, with the stock down about 50% in a month. The administration's 10% stake halved in value, and Dell dropped 16% after Intel's PC warning.

14.text: The articles focus on NVIDIA stock, not Intel, and provide no concrete Intel developments. They only bear on Intel indirectly by covering the AI chip stock rally in which Intel is a peripheral player.

9.text: Qualcomm’s fiscal Q4 earnings fell 28% on handset weakness and rising costs, while Micron guided to its biggest quarter ever but its stock has dropped over 40% since June. The articles focus on Qualcomm, Micron, AMD, and Nvidia, with no concrete Intel developments reported.

5.text: Chip stocks fell sharply on midterm election results that raised fears of slower AI data-center spending, with Intel down 8% on Nov 5 and more than 50% since October. They rebounded partially on Nov 6, led by AMD, Micron, Nvidia and SanDisk.
